q-167818.worked_solution:
To find the coordinates of the point, we inspect its position along the $x$- and $y$-axes.

- The point is $1$ unit to the *right* of the origin, in the *positive* direction of the $x$-axis. So, its $x$-coordinate is $1.$

- The point is $4$ units *below* the origin, in the *negative* direction of the $y$-axis. So, its $y$-coordinate is $-4.$

Therefore, the coordinates of our point are $(1,-4).$

q-167822.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=3.$

Substituting $m=3$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=3x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(1,-4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x+b \\ -4 & =3(1)+b \\ -4 & =3+b \\ -7 & =b \\ b & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=3x-7.
$$

Previously, we found that $\overset{↔}{AB}$ has equation

$$

$$

At the $x$-intercept, the $y$-coordinate is equal to $0.$ So, we can substitute $y=0$ into the equation and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x-7 \\ 0 & =3x-7 \\ 7 & =3x \\ \frac{7}{3} & =\frac{3x}{3} \\ \frac{7}{3} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $x=\frac{7}{3}.$ The coordinates of the $x$-intercept are $(\frac{7}{3},0).$

q-167827.worked_solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other. Therefore, since $\overset{↔}{AB}$ has the slope $m=3,$ our perpendicular line must have a slope of 

$$
{m}_{1}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

So, our perpendicular line has the slope ${m}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}$ and passes through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(6,2).$ 

Finally, using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & ={m}_{1}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =-\frac{1}{3}(x-6) \\ y-2 & =-\frac{1}{3}x+2 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+4\end{aligned}
$$
